Issue: 565
Summary: OpENer commit 76b95cf is reported to have incorrect access control in encapsulation-session handling. In encap.c, CheckRegisteredSessions() checks whether a supplied session_handle is active in the global session list, but not whether that handle belongs to the TCP socket that sent the request. The report says this weak check is used on critical command paths such as SendRRData and SendUnitData, and that UnregisterSession also tears down session resources based only on the handle. A request sent on one connection with another client's valid session_handle can therefore pass session validation. The provided observations show the attacker PoC enumerating/using a valid victim handle, then sending a forged UnregisterSession that the server accepts, destroying the session and forcefully closing the legitimate client's TCP socket. The report also describes this as session hijacking and cross-connection DoS; the demonstrated result shown is the forced disconnect of the legitimate client.
Reproduce: Use an OpENer target at commit 76b95cf; the document does not provide server build commands. Have a legitimate client already connected with an active encapsulation session; the report names the normal client as normal_client.py. Run the provided Python attacker PoC against the ENIP listener (defaults: --host 127.0.0.1, --port 44818, --timeout 1.5). The attacker connects, can optionally call RegisterSession on its own socket (--register-attacker), and then probes candidate handles by sending SendRRData with a benign Get_Attributes_All CIP payload. [SOURCE id=issue:567:567-summary:1255c28909d7 kind=issue issue=567 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#567.txt]
Issue: 567
Summary: On the latest master branch of OpENer, the report describes a remotely reachable server-side crash triggered by a crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request. The report attributes the underlying corruption to request handling before the visible crash: CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure() accepts a malformed CPF with an invalid item_count/inconsistent length, the unconnected Message Router payload reaches GetAttributeList(), GetAttributeList() parses an attacker-controlled excessively large attribute_count_request and builds an oversized inner Message Router response, and EncodeMessageRouterResponseData() copies that inner response into the outer ENIPMessage without validating remaining destination capacity. According to the report, this overruns message_buffer[512] and overwrites the adjacent current_message_position field; the observed result is that AddIntToMessage() later dereferences the corrupted pointer and crashes. The documented crash is an AddressSanitizer SEGV caused by a READ in AddIntToMessage() at source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c:136.
Reproduce: 1) Use the latest master branch of OpENer and run a server instance; the report demonstrates the issue on an AddressSanitizer-instrumented POSIX OpENer build. 2) Send the provided crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request to the server. The PoC is the hex byte sequence beginning with <6f><00><30><01><30><30><30><30> and continuing exactly as provided in the document. 3) Observe the server abort under AddressSanitizer with a SEGV caused by a READ in AddIntToMessage() at source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c:136:49, with the stack including EncodeSockaddrInfoItemTypeId(), AssembleLinearMessage(), NotifyCommonPacketFormat(), HandleReceivedSendRequestResponseDataCommand(), and HandleReceivedExplictTcpData().
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:cve-2020-13556:cve-2020-13556-summa:8e380334c121 kind=issue issue=2020 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#CVE-2020-13556.txt]
Issue: CVE-2020-13556
Summary: OpENer 2.3 and development commit 8c73bf3 have an out-of-bounds write in the Ethernet/IP server functionality, in source/src/enet_encap/cpf.c within CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure. The function reads item_count from an ENIP packet and uses it as a loop counter; during that loop, GetIntFromMessage reads two bytes, converts them to a short integer, and writes it into an array in common_packet_format_data, corresponding to the global g_common_packet_format_data_item, without validating that item_count stays within the valid address_info_item entries. A specially crafted sequence of network requests with an oversized item_count causes the loop to continue past valid entries, resulting in out-of-bounds reads and writes. The document states the write begins at g_common_packet_format_data_item in the .bss segment, can overwrite the heap, and could lead to remote code execution.
Reproduce: The document does not provide a full PoC, build configuration, or commands. The described reproduction is to run an affected OpENer 2.3 or development commit 8c73bf3 Ethernet/IP server and send a specially crafted sequence of ENIP network requests. In the request processed by CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure, set the ENIP packet's item_count field larger than the number of valid address_info_item entries. As the loop continues, GetIntFromMessage keeps reading two-byte values and writing them into the common_packet_format_data / g_common_packet_format_data_item array past its bounds. Expected result: out-of-bounds read/write starting at g_common_packet_format_data_item in the .bss segment; the document says this can overwrite the heap and could lead to remote code execution.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:582:582-summary:a17fd2adbb9f kind=issue issue=582 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#582.txt]
Issue: 582
Summary: OpENer 2.3.0 (commit 76b95cf) has an out-of-bounds read in CIP message parsing when handling malformed explicit requests with a forged EPath size. An ENIP SendRRData request can carry a very short CIP payload whose attacker-controlled path_size claims more path words than are actually available; because the parser continues decoding path segments without a remaining-length boundary, it reads past the end of the stack receive buffer. The report states this is remotely triggerable via network traffic and does not require authentication.
Reproduce: Use the provided Python 3 PoC against a target listening on 127.0.0.1:44818 by default (defaults: attempts=1, timeout=1.5, interval_ms=0, path_words=240, buffer_size=512). The client opens a TCP connection, sends ENIP RegisterSession (0x0065) with payload <HH>(1,0), and extracts the returned session ID. It then sends ENIP SendRRData (0x006F) for that session with 6 zero command-specific bytes plus a CPF whose item count is 3, containing a Null Address item (0x0000, length 0) and an Unconnected Data item (0x00B2) whose declared data length is only 2 bytes: service 0x0E followed by a forged path_size byte set to the requested path_words value. The PoC then appends repeated 0x20 0x01 bytes after that declared payload until the whole packet reaches 512 bytes, sends it, and waits for a reply. Reported outcomes are either RESP - response_len=... or FAIL - no response (reset, crash, or ASan abort), or an exception.
[/SOURCE]
